reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the proposed feedback loop. E2 mentions an oxide film improving wear resistance but not its disruption or galvanic effects. E4 describes pitting corrosion of passive films but in a static, non-wear context. E3 confirms oxide formation at 900°C but not its removal by wear. The core premises of wear-induced oxide removal, galvanic coupling, and feedback are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Wear disrupts a protective oxide film on the alloy surface.
Disrupted oxide exposes heterogeneous surfaces, creating local galvanic cells.
Galvanic corrosion further weakens or prevents oxide reformation.
This creates a positive feedback loop accelerating overall degradation.
The alloy forms a protective oxide film during high-temperature exposure.
